newsitem.title: USA: Rhythm-blues veteran LaVern Baker dead at 67 - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Rhythm-blues veteran LaVern Baker dead at 67 - NYT.

text.p: LaVern Baker, one of the most influential rhythm-and-blues singers of the 1950s, has died of heart complications, the New York Times reported on Wednesday.
The report said the 67-year-old singer died on Monday at St. Luke's-Roosevelt Hospital in Manhattan.

Baker, a Chicago native whose original name was Delores Williams, was a mainstay of Atlantic Records in the mid-1950s. Her hits included "Tweedlee Dee" and "Jim Dandy," which sold a million copies after its 1957 release, the paper said.

After a period of obscurity in the 1960s, she appeared at New York's Madison Square Garden in 1988 for a 40th anniversary concert for Atlantic Records and was chosen to perform in the Broadway show, "Black and Blue."
In 1990, Baker received a career achievement award from the Rhythm-and-Blues Foundation and in 1991 she was inducted into the Rock-and-Roll Hall of Fame, the paper said.
